scope: Twelve source-listed August FDA approval action dates, not all original August PDUFA goals and not an exhaustive set of FDA CRLs, delays, withdrawals, and other August outcomes.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: P304 large Phase 3 vaccine efficacy research reported 26.6% relative efficacy versus licensed standard-dose influenza vaccine in adults at least 50 years old; older-adult immunogenicity data provide a second pathway. Primary source quantities and locked estimates not independently reproduced.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Benefit supported by pivotal seasonal influenza observations; earlier comparator-choice refusal-to-file raises important regulatory risk, and vaccine reactogenicity and rare-event surveillance need independent review.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: March 2026 FDA reconsideration and June 18 advisory committee's favorable vote support an approval lean, while 65+ postmarketing commitments and February filing dispute remain critical qualification.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Comparator standard-of-care dispute, regulatory pathway by age and long-term safety.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: FirstLight and RadiantLight global Phase 3 studies reported improvement in objective wakefulness, cataplexy, and patient-centered outcomes for narcolepsy type 1; precise multiplicity hierarchy requires SAP.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Mechanistically aligned orexin receptor agonism with strong reported symptoms; urinary urgency and insomnia, rare-event safety and long-term exposure still need review.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: FDA priority review of first-in-class narcolepsy type 1 program and two positive Phase 3 studies support approval lean; not evidence of a validated FDA probability.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Original SAP, safety narratives, pivotal population reconciliation and labeling.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: Single-arm Phase 1/2 IGNYTE reported response signal in advanced melanoma; randomized Phase 3 confirmatory results were not mature. Response adjudication and lack of same-study comparator are major limitations.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Unmet need and durable response signals favor a regulatory-flexibility argument, but heterogeneity, surgical response confounding and absence of treatment-contribution evidence remain serious.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: Conservative CRL lean despite July 30 advisory committee 10-to-3 supportive vote, because July 2025 and April 2026 FDA CRLs identified unresolved reliability and attribution issues. A flexible accelerated approval decision remained possible.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Whether FDA would override unresolved efficacy design concerns and require confirmatory Phase 3; CMC commitments.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: Two pivotal tau PET diagnostic studies reportedly met coprimary sensitivity and specificity endpoints; this diagnostic program is not a conventional Phase 3 therapeutic efficacy trial.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Potential to identify tau pathology in cognitive impairment, but quantitative cutoff, reader reproducibility, clinical-use limitations and manufacturing remain open.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: October 2025 accepted NDA with August 13 goal and successful imaging endpoints support a cautious approval lean; no assumption of expanded Alzheimer diagnostic indications.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Original sensitivity/specificity estimates, reader reproducibility and radiotracer manufacturing.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: Randomized staged EXCALIBER-RRMM provides pivotal multiple-myeloma framework. This dated FDA acceptance announcement did not establish full 2026 clinical endpoints or outcomes, which must not be copied from approval-day releases.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Unmet need after prior therapy and CELMoD biologic rationale; hematologic toxicity, infections and reliability of MRD surrogate remain unreviewed.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: FDA breakthrough and priority review favor an approval lean, but this remains low-confidence because the complete predecision efficacy disclosure was not independently available in the cited announcement.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Pivotal trial prespecified primary endpoint, 2026 preapproval MRD evidence, PFS, infections and FDA acceptance details.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: Randomized Phase 3 DTX401-CL301 studied gene therapy in GSDIa; sponsor described pivotal improvement in cornstarch-management burden and additional phase evidence, not independently recreated here.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Important unmet disease-modifying need; AAV gene-transfer hepatic, immune and long-term integration risk and very small rare-disease samples require safety scrutiny.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: FDA priority review, positive reported Phase 3 and strong unmet need support conditional accelerated-approval lean; precise surrogate validation and gene therapy CMC are unresolved.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Exact primary data, planned confirmatory evidence, immune safety, gene-vector CMC and postmarketing requirements.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: OPTIMA Phase 3 63-participant randomized controlled trial reported 90% and 94% reductions in incident heterotopic ossification lesions versus placebo. Doses differed in secondary flare-up significance.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Strong primary signal in ultra-rare FOP against dose-related soft-tissue infection concerns, small samples and no independently demonstrated durable functional improvement.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: Original Phase 3 primary endpoint positivity and large effect in disease with major unmet need support approval lean despite small samples and safety uncertainty.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Exact multiplicity across two doses, infection definitions, durability, CMC and labeling restrictions.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: Randomized three-arm HERIZON-GEA-01 with favorable PFS for both investigational regimens; OS benefit supported tislelizumab-containing combination, with chemotherapy-only combination's OS still less mature at initial review.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: HER2 targeted first-line gastric/esophageal disease benefit versus diarrhea, cardiac toxicity and immunotherapy safety; companion diagnostic subgroup boundaries matter.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: Established 2024 Ziihera monotherapy authorization and positive 2025/2026 Phase 3 results favor first-line supplemental approval lean, without using August 31 postapproval update.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: OS analysis hierarchy for two regimens, HER2 IHC 2+/ISH+ scope and cardiac safety.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: Randomized Phase 3 RASolute 302 showed sponsor-reported substantial overall survival improvement versus chemotherapy for metastatic pancreatic cancer; source says all principal endpoints positive but independently frozen figures not replayed.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Important direct survival endpoint and severe unmet need, with potential gastrointestinal toxicity, dose interruptions and subgroup heterogeneity requiring review.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: July 2026 FDA NDA acceptance and clinically meaningful OS signal favor approval lean. August action was unusually early relative to subsequently reported 2027 target; do not infer timing skill.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Original public timing of detailed OS publication, clinical SAP, safety/CMC, and original FDA goal-date identity.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: Phase 3 VALOR 52-week placebo-controlled dermatomyositis trial achieved its primary endpoint and supported priority review, according to sponsor.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Potential first targeted adult dermatomyositis treatment, balanced against class JAK/TYK2 immunosuppression and thromboembolic infection concerns.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: Positive pivotal trial and accepted priority-review NDA in high unmet-need indication favor approval lean, with major safety warning risks.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Original endpoint/effect, missing data, long-term infection/thrombosis and full risk labeling.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: ARTISTRY-1 and ARTISTRY-2 Phase 3 trials reported comparable maintenance of HIV suppression through 48 weeks with once-daily oral BIC/LEN in previously suppressed adults.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Switch-regimen convenience with integrase and capsid mechanism precedent, while resistance, drug-drug interactions and long-term adherence safety remain concerns.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: Priority review and reported virologic noninferiority favor approval for a restricted already-suppressed population, not treatment-naive HIV patients.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Noninferiority margins, resistance subgroups, neuropsychiatric events and combination label.

datedPublicEvidence.clinical: Phase 3 VERIFY rusfertide plus standard of care more than doubled clinical response rates on hematocrit control and phlebotomy reduction, according to dated issuer disclosure.
datedPublicEvidence.benefitRisk: Direct hematocrit control and patient fatigue improvement with injection-site reactions and anemia; disease complication risk and overall safety need independent analysis.
datedPublicEvidence.regulatory: Positive VERIFY trial, Breakthrough/Fast Track/Orphan designations and FDA priority review support approval lean.
datedPublicEvidence.unresolved: Actual treatment-group response CI, missingness, thrombosis/iron deficiency and postapproval safety.

monthOverlap: Do not merge August action-date reviews with September and October original-goal-date calendar without exact application-cycle de-duplication.
